questions.q: What did the story of psychologist Takeo Doi illustrate about social skills?
a: Different cultures teach different levels of sensitivity to others’ needs
Guests should always accept food when it is offered
Language barriers make reading people impossible
Politeness is universal and means the same thing everywhere
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts American hosts who asked about food with Japanese hosts who would notice cues and offer without asking.

questions.q: What did the 2004 study on squirrel monkeys suggest about moderate childhood stress?
a: It can sharpen social skills later in life
It permanently damages the ability to bond
It has no effect on behavior either way
It makes animals avoid unfamiliar environments
questions.why: Lesson 1 says mild stress in childhood increased the monkeys’ courage to explore and, by extension, openness to others.

questions.q: What did research on women caring for partners with Alzheimer’s find?
a: Constant caregiving weakened the caretakers’ immune systems
Caregiving had no measurable effect on health
Caretakers became more patient over time
Caretakers slept better than other women
questions.why: Lesson 2 reports that prolonged care work worsened mental health and weakened the carers’ immune systems.

questions.q: What does Goleman recommend for people overwhelmed by caring for someone?
a: Share the responsibility across a wider community of family and friends
Take a long break from all social contact
Hire professional help and step back entirely
Reduce the amount of care the person receives
questions.why: Lesson 2 says one person has biological limits, so a group should share care, which also builds new bonds.

questions.q: Why do Indian hospitals in the summary not serve meals to patients?
a: To ensure family and friends visit and keep patients socially involved
To save money for more advanced medical equipment
To encourage patients to eat healthier food at home
To reduce the workload of hospital kitchen staff
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the practice brings visitors who deliver food, which supports recovery through social contact.
